paper_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

sub_questions.q: What is the title of the paper and what is the paper's proposed model called?
sub_questions.answer: The paper is titled "Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models," and the proposed model is abbreviated as AWD-LSTM for ASGD Weight-Dropped LSTM.
sub_questions.quote: In the results, we abbreviate our approach as AWD-LSTM for ASGD Weight-Dropped LSTM.

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity does the paper report on Penn Treebank for the paper's proposed AWD-LSTM model as a single model without cache/pointer?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports a Penn Treebank test perplexity of 57.3 for AWD-LSTM, a 3-layer LSTM with tied weights, as a single model without cache/pointer.
sub_questions.quote: Using these and other regularization strategies, we achieve state-of-the-art word level perplexities on two data sets: 57.3 on Penn Treebank and 65.8 on WikiText-2.

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity does the paper report on Penn Treebank for the proposed model when augmented with a continuous cache pointer?
sub_questions.answer: With a continuous cache pointer, the paper reports an even lower Penn Treebank test perplexity of 52.8.
sub_questions.quote: In exploring the effectiveness of a neural cache in conjunction with our proposed model, we achieve an even lower state-of-the-art perplexity of 52.8 on Penn Treebank and 52.0 on WikiText-2.

sub_questions.q: In what evaluation setting are the Penn Treebank results reported: single model, with dynamic evaluation, with cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning?
sub_questions.answer: The Penn Treebank table is explicitly captioned as single model perplexity on validation and test sets. The paper reports a continuous cache pointer variant, and fine-tuning is part of the training procedure, but the provided paper text does not report dynamic evaluation or ensemble results.
sub_questions.quote: Single model perplexity on validation and test sets for the Penn Treebank language modeling task.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper's reported Penn Treebank test perplexity include fine-tuning, and what does the no-fine-tuning ablation report?
sub_questions.answer: The main 57.3 Penn Treebank test perplexity includes the fine-tuning step. Table 4 lists the no-fine-tuning ablation as 58.8 test perplexity on Penn Treebank, showing removal degrades performance.
sub_questions.quote: Similarly, the removal of the fine-tuning step expectedly also degrades the performance.

sub_questions.q: How does the proposed model's Penn Treebank test perplexity compare with the baselines listed in the paper?
sub_questions.answer: The paper states its vanilla LSTM improves the state of the art by approximately 1 unit on Penn Treebank. In Table 1, AWD-LSTM's 57.3 beats the best listed baseline, Melis et al. 2017 4-layer skip connection LSTM (tied) at 58.3, while many other baselines are higher; with the continuous cache pointer, 52.8 is even lower.
sub_questions.quote: On both data sets we improve the state-of-the-art, with our vanilla LSTM model beating the state of the art by approximately 1 unit on PTB and 0.1 units on WT2.
